statement: I want to operate the controls I use most often without taking my eyes off the road.
rationale: Independent testing finds flush, unlit and touch-only controls force the driver to look away to adjust common functions.
customer_context: Daily driving, adjusting climate and media while moving.

statement: I want to keep the big, clear screen and still have the everyday controls be easy to use while driving.
rationale: The curved display and interaction surfaces are received as premium and modern, while the control layer around them is what testers criticise. The screen is not the problem and should not be sacrificed to fix the controls.
customer_context: Daily driving; also the showroom impression that sells the car.

statement: I want to put the functions I personally use most within one deliberate reach.
rationale: Assignable favourite buttons were removed and are missed; shortcut access reduces menu hunting for individual habits.
customer_context: Repeat journeys where the same few functions are used every time.

statement: I want the car's digital experience to get better while I own it, not fall behind.
rationale: Competitors sell infotainment compute upgrades and full over-the-air updates, setting an expectation of post-purchase improvement.
customer_context: Multi-year ownership, comparing against newer cars.

statement: I want to know up front which digital features stay free and which I will be asked to pay for later.
rationale: Connected services lapse into paid tiers and some conveniences are cost options.
customer_context: End of the included service period.

statement: I want a long-distance charging stop to take about as long as I was told it would.
rationale: Peak power is competitive but tapers early, so session averages and real stop times fall well short of the headline figure.
customer_context: Autobahn trips with one or two planned charging stops.

statement: I want to know how much usable range a stop will actually give me, in kilometres.
rationale: Range recovered per stop is the figure customers plan around; 184 km in 20 minutes is more meaningful to them than a kilowatt peak.
customer_context: Trip planning before and during a journey.

statement: I do not want to pay for energy that never reaches my battery.
rationale: Independent testers judge charging losses improvable and include them in measured consumption.
customer_context: Every charging session, especially on public DC pricing.

statement: I want one simple way to find, use and pay for charging wherever I am.
rationale: Single-app access across a broad provider network is positioned as a strength and matches how customers want to charge.
customer_context: Charging away from home on mixed networks.

statement: I want the range the car promises to be the range I get.
rationale: Measured consumption of 27.1 kWh/100 km against a 14.7 kWh/100 km catalogue figure is the mechanism behind range disappointment.
customer_context: Winter, autobahn and fully loaded driving.

statement: I want a comfortable ride without having to find the right expensive option box.
rationale: The Sport-package suspension is judged too firm for comfortable family use, with ride only improving noticeably on a costly adaptive option.
customer_context: Family and long-distance use on imperfect German roads.

statement: I want the surfaces I touch every day to feel as premium as the car's price implies.
rationale: Independent review calls specific details not very premium-like, naming piano-black surfaces and cheap-feeling door touch buttons.
customer_context: Every entry and exit; daily contact points.

statement: I want space for four adults and their luggage without compromise.
rationale: Measured legroom, headroom and boot volume are a recognised multi-generation strength, and the segment is competing on exactly this.
customer_context: Family trips and business travel with passengers.

statement: I want the car to go exactly where I point it, including at speed on a rutted road.
rationale: Base steering is judged vague with rear-axle steering credited for the necessary bite, and owners report tramlining on large wheels.
customer_context: Autobahn cruising and winding secondary roads.

statement: I want an electric car that still carries what my estate carries today.
rationale: The Touring body is popular in Germany while electric estates remain rare, so the demand pocket is underserved.
customer_context: German buyers replacing a combustion estate.
